text: Code refactoring means improving the structure of existing code without changing what it does. The goal is to make code easier to read, understand, and maintain. Developers often refactor when they notice messy or confusing parts of a program. This process helps reduce technical debt, which builds up when code is written quickly without much care. By cleaning up the code, teams can fix problems faster and add new features more easily. Refactoring is not about adding new functionality; it is about making the code better on the inside while keeping the same behavior on the outside.
